syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

topics.title: Background: the author and the Franco-Prussian War

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the historical setting of the story: France's defeat in the Franco-Prussian War and the passing of Alsace and Lorraine to Prussia.
Identify the author, the narrator and the point of view from which the story is told.

topics.title: Franz's morning: temptation, dread and the bulletin-board

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Franz's fear of a scolding and the temptations he resisted on his way to school.
Interpret the significance of the crowd at the town-hall bulletin-board and Wachter's remark.

topics.title: The unusual classroom: stillness, M. Hamel's dress and the village elders

concepts.learning_objective: Analyse how the silence of the classroom and M. Hamel's special clothes signal a solemn occasion.
Explain why old Hauser and the other villagers sat on the back benches.

topics.title: The order from Berlin and M. Hamel's message on language

concepts.learning_objective: State the order from Berlin and its effect on the school.
Evaluate M. Hamel's view that everyone, including himself, was to blame for putting off learning.
Interpret M. Hamel's idea that holding fast to one's language is like holding the key to one's prison.

topics.title: The last lessons and M. Hamel's farewell

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the writing lesson, M. Hamel's last moments in the classroom and his farewell.
Interpret Franz's thought about the pigeons being made to sing in German.

topics.title: Working with words and noticing form

concepts.learning_objective: Infer the meanings of expressions such as 'thunderclap', 'in unison' and 'in plenty of time' from the context.
Recognise that English has borrowed words from many languages, as shown in the chapter's examples.
Identify the past perfect form in the story and explain its use to show an earlier past.

topics.title: Saheb, his name and the author's hollow promise
topics.ncert_sections: Sometimes I find a Rupee in the garbage (opening)

concepts.learning_objective: Recall where Saheb came from and why his family migrated to the city.
Explain how casual promises to poor children reflect the bleakness of their world.
Interpret the irony of the name Saheb-e-Alam.

topics.title: Barefoot children: tradition or poverty
topics.ncert_sections: Sometimes I find a Rupee in the garbage (barefoot boys; the Udipi story)

concepts.learning_objective: Evaluate the explanations offered for children going barefoot.
Interpret what the Udipi temple story shows about change and lasting poverty.

topics.title: Seemapuri and the life of ragpickers
topics.ncert_sections: Sometimes I find a Rupee in the garbage (Seemapuri)

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the living conditions and status of the ragpickers of Seemapuri.
Compare what garbage means to the children and to the elders of Seemapuri.

topics.title: Saheb at the tennis club and the tea stall
topics.ncert_sections: Sometimes I find a Rupee in the garbage (closing)

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret the tennis shoes and the game as symbols of what is beyond Saheb's reach.
Analyse how a paid job at the tea stall costs Saheb his freedom.

topics.title: Mukesh and the bangle makers of Firozabad
topics.ncert_sections: I want to drive a car (Firozabad and Mukesh's home)

concepts.learning_objective: Identify Firozabad's bangle industry and the hazards of working in it.
Describe Mukesh's home and family and the poverty they live in.
Explain the irony between the sanctity of bangles and the misery of their makers.

topics.title: The vicious circle and Mukesh's dream
topics.ncert_sections: I want to drive a car (closing)

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how belief in destiny and caste keeps the bangle makers in their work.
Analyse the forces that keep the bangle makers trapped in poverty.
Contrast Mukesh's dream with his family's acceptance of their lot.

topics.title: Literary devices and vocabulary in Lost Spring

concepts.learning_objective: Identify hyperbole, simile, metaphor and irony in lines from the text.
Infer the meaning of words and phrases from their context in the text.

topics.title: About the author and the roots of the fear

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the author, the source of the excerpt and the purpose of the essay.
Explain how Douglas's early experiences created an aversion to water.

topics.title: The misadventure in the Y.M.C.A. pool

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the events of the near-drowning and the plan Douglas made to save himself.
Analyse the details that make the description of panic vivid.

topics.title: The lasting effects of the fear

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the immediate physical and emotional effects of the incident.
Explain how the fear of water handicapped Douglas over the years.

topics.title: The instructor builds a swimmer

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the step-by-step method the instructor used to train Douglas.
Evaluate the role of patience and repeated practice in overcoming fear.

topics.title: Testing the victory over fear

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how Douglas tested himself to make sure the terror had gone.
Interpret how Douglas faced the traces of terror that remained.

topics.title: Theme, language and narrative style

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret the larger meaning Douglas draws from conquering fear.
Interpret key words, images and the first-person narrative style.

topics.title: The peddler and his rattrap idea

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the peddler's poverty and way of life at the start of the story.
Explain the peddler's idea that the whole world is a big rattrap and why it pleased him.

topics.title: The crofter's hospitality and the theft

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the lonely old crofter welcomed and confided in the peddler.
Analyse how the peddler betrayed the crofter's trust by stealing the thirty kronor.

topics.title: Lost in the forest and the forge at Ramsjo

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret the peddler's wandering in the forest as his own fall into the rattrap.
Describe the forge at Ramsjo Ironworks and how the blacksmiths received the tramp.

topics.title: Mistaken identity and Edla's invitation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the ironmaster mistook the peddler for an old comrade and why the peddler played along.
Explain how Edla's kindness persuaded the frightened peddler to come to the manor house.

topics.title: Christmas Eve and the truth revealed

concepts.learning_objective: Compare the ironmaster's and Edla's attitudes towards the stranger once the truth comes out.
Interpret the peddler's defence and his warning to the ironmaster about the rattrap.

topics.title: The gift, the letter and redemption

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the meaning of the peddler's parting gift, his letter and his signature.
Evaluate how trust and kindness awaken the essential goodness in the peddler.

topics.title: Language: words and reflexive pronouns

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish the emphatic and the reflexive use of pronouns ending in -self in the story.
Infer the meaning of words and expressions from their context in the story.

topics.title: Rajkumar Shukla and the road to Champaran

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how Rajkumar Shukla's persistence brought Gandhi to Champaran.
Trace Gandhi's journey from Lucknow to Muzaffarpur and explain what it reveals about social attitudes of the time.

topics.title: The indigo sharecropping system

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the 15 per cent indigo arrangement and how synthetic indigo changed it.
Explain why Gandhi held that freedom from fear mattered more to the peasants than law courts.

topics.title: Defiance and trial at Motihari

concepts.learning_objective: Analyse how Gandhi's peaceful defiance at Motihari led to the first triumph of civil disobedience in modern India.
Interpret Gandhi's 'conflict of duties' and his appeal to the voice of conscience.

topics.title: The lawyers' resolve, the inquiry and the settlement

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how Gandhi's example changed the attitude of the Bihar lawyers.
Evaluate why Gandhi accepted a 25 per cent refund and what it achieved for the peasants.

topics.title: Social reform, self-reliance and the Gandhian pattern

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the educational, health and sanitation work Gandhi began in Champaran villages.
Explain the lesson in self-reliance Gandhi taught through the Andrews episode.
Interpret why Champaran was a turning point and how Gandhi's politics were tied to people's daily problems.

topics.title: Vocabulary and language in 'Indigo'

concepts.learning_objective: Identify words related to legal procedures and infer word meanings from context.
Explain the use of direct speech in narration and of the comma with subordinate clauses.

topics.title: The make-up department of Gemini Studios
topics.ncert_sections: Opening section: Pancake, the make-up room and its staff

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the Pancake make-up, the make-up room and the 'fiery misery' of those being made up.
Explain how the mixed staff of the make-up department illustrates national integration.
Interpret the strict hierarchy of the make-up department and the author's ironic view of it.

topics.title: The office boy and the author's work
topics.ncert_sections: The office boy, the author's cubicle and the office boy's frustration

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the office boy joined the studio, why he was frustrated and whom he blamed.
Describe the author's job at Gemini Studios and why others thought he did nothing.

topics.title: Kothamangalam Subbu

concepts.learning_objective: Identify Subbu's many talents as film-maker, poet, novelist and actor.
Describe Subbu's loyalty, generosity and the reasons he had enemies.

topics.title: The Story Department and the legal adviser
topics.ncert_sections: The Story Department, the lawyer and the actress

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the legal adviser unwittingly ended an actress's career.
Interpret the lawyer's isolation among the poets and the irony of his losing his job.

topics.title: Communism and the Moral Re-Armament visit
topics.ncert_sections: The poets' politics and the MRA visit of 1952

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the Gemini poets' notions about Communism and their political outlook.
Explain the MRA's visit, its plays and their influence on Tamil drama.

topics.title: Stephen Spender's visit and the mystery solved
topics.ncert_sections: The English poet's visit, The Encounter and The God That Failed

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the English poet's visit and why it baffled the Gemini staff.
Explain how the author identified Spender and why the visit stopped being a mystery.

topics.title: Humour, style and vocabulary
topics.ncert_sections: Gentle humour, rambling style and words and expressions from the text

concepts.learning_objective: Infer the meaning of expressions such as 'blew over' and 'the favourite haunt' from context.
Analyse how the author uses gentle irony and self-mockery to point out human foibles.

topics.title: The interview as a genre and its divided reputation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the interview has become a commonplace of journalism and why opinions about it vary.
Compare the admiring and hostile views of the interview presented by Silvester.
Explain Denis Brian's view of the interview as a powerful medium of communication.

topics.title: Celebrity writers on being interviewed

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the attitudes of Naipaul, Carroll and Kipling towards interviews.
Analyse the gap between what Kipling and Wells said about interviews and what they did.
Interpret Saul Bellow's image of interviews as thumbprints on his windpipe.

topics.title: Umberto Eco: one purpose and the use of interstices

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how Eco's varied work is unified by the same ethical and philosophical interests.
Interpret what Eco means by working in the interstices of life.

topics.title: Eco's narrative scholarship and his identity as an academic

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how Eco's dissertation led him to write scholarly work as the story of research.
Recall when and how Eco began writing novels, in contrast with Roland Barthes.
Evaluate Eco's view of himself as a professor who writes novels on Sundays.

topics.title: The Name of the Rose and the mystery of its success

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why Eco was not puzzled that a serious novel found a mass audience.
Analyse Eco's argument that the success of a book cannot be predicted.

topics.title: Discourse linkers, signallers and reporting an interview
topics.ncert_sections: Noticing discourse linkers and signallers; Writing

concepts.learning_objective: Identify how reference pronouns and repetition link the turns of a conversation.
Recognise phrases that signal a shift of topic in a conversation.
Transfer the salient points of an interview into a concise report.

topics.title: Sophie's dreams and Jansie's realism

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Sophie's fanciful ambitions and what they reveal about her as a school-leaver.
Contrast Jansie's practical view of their future with Sophie's daydreams.
Identify A. R. Barton's theme of adolescent fantasising and hero worship.

topics.title: Sophie's home and family background

concepts.learning_objective: Infer the family's working-class background from details of their home and talk.
Describe the temperament of Sophie's father and his attitude to her stories.

topics.title: Sophie and her brother Geoff

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Geoff's work and his silent, reserved nature.
Explain why Geoff represents the wider, unknown world that Sophie longs to enter.

topics.title: The Danny Casey story and hero worship

concepts.learning_objective: Recall and evaluate Sophie's account of meeting Danny Casey in the arcade.
Explain how the family's admiration for United and Casey shows hero worship.

topics.title: Waiting by the canal: fantasy and reality

concepts.learning_objective: Trace how Sophie's hope turns into doubt and sadness as she waits by the canal.
Analyse how the ending suggests the meeting with Casey was imagined.

topics.title: Words, expressions and present participles

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the non-literal meaning of expressions used in the story.
Identify present participles used to show two actions happening at the same time.
Give the meaning of informal words such as chuffed, nosey and gawky.

topics.title: Kamala Das and the setting of the poem

concepts.learning_objective: Recall key facts about Kamala Das and recognise the qualities of her writing seen in this poem.
Trace the situation of the poem: the drive from the parents' home to Cochin airport and the parting there.

topics.title: Images of the ageing mother

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret the image of the dozing mother's face, 'ashen like that of a corpse', and the realisation it brings.
Explain why the mother is compared to a 'late winter's moon'.

topics.title: Contrast: young trees and merry children

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the image of the young trees 'sprinting' and what it suggests.
Analyse how the images of youth outside the car contrast with the ageing mother.

topics.title: The parting: fear, smile and the poem's structure

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the 'old familiar ache' as the poet's childhood fear of losing her mother.
Interpret the parting words 'see you soon, Amma' and the repeated smile.
Recognise that the poem is a single sentence and explain the effect of this form.

topics.title: The poet, his purpose and the call to keep still

concepts.learning_objective: Identify Pablo Neruda and the purpose of the poem: quiet introspection and mutual understanding.
Explain why the poet asks everyone to count to twelve, keep still and not speak in any language.
Interpret the 'exotic moment' of togetherness without rush or engines.

topics.title: Harm to nature and to oneself

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the image of fishermen and whales shows man's exploitation of nature.
Interpret how the salt gatherer looking at his hurt hands shows neglected self-awareness.

topics.title: War and universal brotherhood

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret the poet's images of green wars, wars with gas and fire, and 'victory with no survivors'.
Explain how the moment of quiet could turn war-makers towards peace and brotherhood.

topics.title: Stillness is not inactivity: the sadness of not understanding

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that the poet wants introspection, not total inactivity or death.
Identify the 'sadness' of never understanding ourselves and threatening ourselves with death.

topics.title: The Earth as teacher and the form of the poem

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the symbol of the Earth that seems dead and later proves to be alive.
Recognise the poem's free verse, varying line lengths and its framing by the count to twelve.

topics.title: About the poet and the poem

concepts.learning_objective: Recall key facts about John Keats as a British Romantic poet.
Explain the Greek legend of Endymion from which the poem is taken.

topics.title: Beauty as a joy forever

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the poet calls a thing of beauty a joy forever whose loveliness increases.
Interpret the images of the quiet bower and the sleep full of sweet dreams.

topics.title: Beauty in spite of suffering

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the things the poet lists as causes of suffering and gloom.
Interpret the image of wreathing a flowery band that binds us to the earth.
Explain how some shape of beauty moves away the pall from our dark spirits.

topics.title: Nature's things of beauty

concepts.learning_objective: List and interpret the objects of nature the poet calls things of beauty.
Use the meanings of words such as rills, brake and covert to read the nature images.

topics.title: The mighty dead, lovely tales and the endless fountain

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why grandeur is associated with the mighty dead and lovely tales.
Interpret the image of an endless fountain of immortal drink from heaven's brink.
Analyse the poem's rhyming couplets and balanced sentence structure.
